8. The proposed smaller decisive experiment

The priced experiment uses two compatible endpoint crossframes one 0.90 m bay apart, one stationary holder and a shortened main positioner. It contains:

Twelve bar bodies: seven installed and five compatible spares.
Fourteen installed host ports and two spares.
Fourteen installed cartridges and six spares.
Three capture units.
Three finite drive cartridges.
The actual ordinary and exceptional interfaces.
The separate probe, floor handler and restrained rack.

The first crossframe is independently anchored before the interval. The completed one-bay cantilever must retain a real 100 N load after every construction tool withdraws.

The proposed autonomous block contains at least 120 reusable operations, two loaded captured failures, placement recovery, a partly completed cup stroke and a failed first drive spare. Fault placement is restricted to the actual compatible stock. A slack, independently load-sensed safety catch may be present; any significant catch load invalidates unsupported acceptance.

Itemized build budget
Group	Cost
Structural and connector stock	$43,000
Service heads, interchangeable drives and capture units	$52,000
Short main positioner	$52,000
Stationary holder	$56,000
Independent floor handler	$38,900
Empty-tool coupling, adapters and yoke	$23,000
Factory-frame yoke and root nutrunner	$32,000
Restrained rack and receiver	$60,960
Separate probe, berth and index-proof hardware	$31,100
Prepared metrology, acquisition, controls and calibration	$58,000
Mechanical and software preparation	$73,200
Anchored setup, shoring, fault specimens and integration	$30,000
Total	$550,160

The separate $11,048.80 campaign allowance includes observation labor, pre/post inspection and stock restoration, a competent matched operator, laboratory access, rejected specimens, waste handling, 80 kWh of process-electricity allowance and 160 kWh of separately metered facility electricity.

Independent measurements must include both pin-plane forces, remote shank strain, individual support reactions, actual gaps, frame displacement/rotation, screw travel, rotor speed, brake temperature, gas/oil pressure and grid electricity. Dynamic release measurements require at least 2 kHz independent acquisition; the proposed terminal energy witness has its own higher-rate requirement.
